output.summary: Separate standalone analyzer predicates and commit-derived parameters from runtime facts collected by G2. Bind and validate the actual profile, inventory and baseline through independently registered collectors before using a conditional sparse result.

findings.impact: The analyzer cannot construct a valid usable conditional report for its stated CLI, so practical sparse execution may be impossible or require unverifiable guessed expectations.
findings.text: The v2 report requires an `expected` value for each singleton including actual runner/profile, discovered inventory and compatible baseline receipt identity, but the documented `trail impact` invocation provides only two commit arguments and schema version; G1 cannot determine which G2 profile, inventory or local receipt will be used. Define a machine-readable registry predicate/descriptor for execution-only facts that G2 independently binds and verifies, or a supported explicit context input with strict validation, and distinguish analyzer-known facts from consumer evidence. Test standalone analyzer invocation followed by a real matching G2 conditional sparse run and forged/mismatched values.

output.summary: Registry predicates separate analyzer-known facts from independently observed execution evidence.

findings.impact: The analyzer cannot enable sparse execution for any normal repository, even with identical endpoints and a compatible passing baseline.
findings.response: disputed: Identical populated Git trees now analyze inputs and return complete when no actual gaps exist. Changed trees still require unbounded fallback because callbacks, resources, dynamic dispatch and cross-file resolution remain unmodeled; treating those relationships as complete would violate the approved design. No unsupported scope is claimed.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts unconditionally emits an unbounded gap for every changed tree and every identical nonempty tree. Implement justified supported completeness or bounded scopes, including a valid unchanged populated tree, rather than always forcing full-profile fallback.

findings.impact: A changed ESM parser runtime can retain the same grammar identity and cache key, replaying extraction facts from a different runtime.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts grammarIdentity hashes createRequire.resolve("web-tree-sitter"), the CJS entrypoint, but src/graph/wasm-runtime.ts dynamically imports the distinct ESM entrypoint web-tree-sitter.js for breadth/container parsing. Hash the actual loaded runtime or otherwise version all parsing inputs.

findings.impact: The required extraction cache is unavailable on a supported platform, hurting repeated-run performance and breaking the packaged distribution test there.
findings.text: src/impact/analyze.ts extractionCache tests POSIX group/other mode bits on all platforms. On Windows libuv synthesizes those bits for ordinary writable directories and does not model NTFS ACL privacy, so the parent check rejects cache creation and the packed cache test fails. Use a Windows-appropriate secure cache design and verify on Windows.

findings.impact: A malformed or partially recovered source tree can be asserted to have complete conditional dependency coverage, allowing the consumer to exclude tests despite analysis of an incomplete or incorrect syntax tree.
findings.text: src/impact/node-static.ts certifies tree-sitter trees without rejecting parse errors or missing tokens. A changed commit with `export function a() { return 2;` and no closing brace produces schema v2 conditional with no gap or fallback, although tsc reports TS1005. Reject malformed/recovered trees for both endpoints.

findings.impact: The test suite passes while the analyzer incorrectly reports conditional completeness for syntactically invalid committed inputs.
findings.text: test/impact-conditional-contract.test.ts does not cover missing anonymous syntax tokens or other tree-sitter recovery shapes. Add a real-CLI regression with a missing closing brace (and both endpoints as appropriate) requiring an unbounded gap and full fallback.

output.summary: The v2 certifier must reject recovered syntax errors before reporting conditional completeness.
Parser recovery tests cover malformed old and new revisions with mandatory full fallback.

spec: Implement conservative impact analysis directly in this Trail-code fork specified in docs/test-impact/design.md, sections 1–6, 8, 11–13 and delivery steps 1–2. Use upstream base ca20a67764e99531a1cf272eea8354e2c16f71d9 and define versioned impact contracts and exact explicit endpoints. Analyze both snapshots, preserve ambiguity and analysis gaps, traverse complete reverse dependencies without arbitrary limits, handle deletions, renames and rebinding, and isolate and validate conservative caches. Report justified fallback scopes instead of silently omitting uncertainty. Include meaningful tests for endpoint semantics, graph completeness, gaps, cache freshness and representative dependency cases. Preserve upstream licensing and document the pinned source. Do not implement a replacement parser or assume normal navigation output is conservative. The full design and its acceptance matrix are binding; resolve open distribution and interface choices through the workflow. Work directly in this fork for a future upstream pull request; no separate test-impact repository or Git subtree. Preserve the separate Unity plugin branch. Where the design refers to a separate fork and adapter distribution, adapt it to this unified repository. Owner scope clarification: Initial release requires explicit committed Git endpoints only, and must work across platforms and filesystems with ordinary Git repositories, without Btrfs, privileged operations, special mounts or subvolumes. Worktree target support is deferred; reject it clearly rather than silently substituting a commit. Preserve exact target execution identity and protection against mutations, and adapt the original worktree-specific acceptance cases accordingly.
